Convert a saved Google Scholar results page to BibTeX

Source: R/scholar.R
scholar_html_to_bib.Rd

Parses a saved Scholar results page with [scholar_parse_html()] and writes BibTeX entries. Results with a venue become `@article`; others become `@misc`. Entries whose author list or venue was cut short by Scholar get a `note` field saying so, so you can find and complete them.

Usage

scholar_html_to_bib(
  input,
  output = NULL,
  drop_duplicates = TRUE,
  abstracts = FALSE,
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OPENALEX_API_KEY")
)

Arguments

input

One or more paths to saved `.html` files, **a folder** (every `.html` / `.htm` file in it is read), or a string of HTML text. Results from several pages are combined.

output

Path for the `.bib` file. If `NULL` (default), nothing is written and the entries are returned.

drop_duplicates

Remove results that appear more than once (same title, case ignored) when you combine several pages.

abstracts

If `TRUE`, look up each abstract in OpenAlex with [fetch_abstracts()] and include it in the entries. Needs internet access.

api_key

Your OpenAlex API key, passed to [fetch_abstracts()]. Defaults to the `OPENALEX_API_KEY` environment variable.

Value

A character vector with one BibTeX entry per result (invisibly when `output` is given).

Details

The entries only contain what the results list shows (no volume, pages, DOI or abstract). For complete records use Scholar's Cite > BibTeX.

Examples

page <- '<div class="gs_r"><div class="gs_ri">
  <h3 class="gs_rt"><a href="https://example.org/a">Retention and advising</a></h3>
  <div class="gs_a">A Smith, B Jones - Journal of Examples, 2019 - Example Press</div>
  </div></div>'
cat(scholar_html_to_bib(page))
#> @article{smith2019retention,
#>   author    = {Smith, A. and Jones, B.},
#>   title     = {{Retention and advising}},
#>   journal   = {Journal of Examples},
#>   year      = 2019,
#>   publisher = {Example Press},
#>   url       = {https://example.org/a}
#> }
